I have farmed these 10.1 mu in Quzhou for 35 years. Never went to school. My wife and I do the field work, and my son works in the city sending money home. I don't read books and I don't trust new ideas unless I see them work on Old Wang's field next door. Last year my wheat gave me about 500 jin per mu and my maize gave me over 600 jin. That was not a great year but it was enough. So this year I will do almost the same thing, because change is risky and a bad harvest means borrowing money.

For wheat: I plant the improved variety that Old Wang has been using for three years. I buy about 150 jin of seed for the whole 10.1 mu. In October after the maize comes off, I rotary till the ground. At planting I spread one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu, the big bag that weighs 50 kilograms. In March when the wheat turns green, I spread one bag of urea per mu, the 40-kilogram bag. Two years ago I tried to save money and only used half a bag of urea, and the wheat turned yellow and thin. The yield dropped. Never again. I would rather waste some fertilizer than lose a whole crop. I irrigate four times: winter water before the ground freezes, green-up water in early spring, jointing water when the stems shoot up, and grain-filling water in May if the sky stays dry. I spray herbicide once and insecticide once, so two pesticide applications total. I expect 550 kilograms per mu if the weather is normal.

For maize: I plant hybrid seed, the kind the dealer sells in the red package. I use about 3 jin per mu. Right after wheat harvest in June, I don't till the ground much, I plant straight into the wheat stubble — no-tillage. At sowing I put 40 kilograms of compound fertilizer per mu in the rows. When the plants are knee-high, at the big trumpet stage, I topdress with 25 kilograms of urea per mu. Last year I did exactly this and the cobs were thick and heavy. I irrigate twice: once right after sowing if the soil is dry, and once at the big trumpet stage. I spray for weeds once and for corn borer once, so two pesticide times. I expect 650 kilograms per mu.

Fertilizer is expensive now. One bag of urea costs over 100 yuan, more than five years ago. But I have 10.1 mu, which is not tiny, so I can handle the cost if I am careful and don't hire extra labor. I watch what Old Wang does. If he puts on more this year, I might add a little too. But for now I stick with what I know.
